questions.q: What is personal selling?
options: A face-to-face sales presentation to a prospective customer
questions.explain: It allows detailed explanations and answers to objections.
questions.evidence: Personal selling is a face-to-face sales presentation to a prospective customer.

questions.q: What is an advantage of personal selling over advertising?
options: It reaches millions of people at once
The salesperson can answer the prospect's own questions and objections
questions.explain: Advertising can only respond to objections the copywriter anticipated.
questions.evidence: Moreover, when the prospect has questions or raises objections, the salesperson is there to provide explanations.

questions.q: What is prospecting?
options: Looking for the companies and people most likely to buy the seller's offerings
questions.explain: It is the first step of the selling process.
questions.evidence: These steps are as follows: Prospecting and qualifying: To start the process, the salesperson looks for sales prospects, those companies and people who are most likely to buy the seller’s offerings.

questions.q: Why do salespeople qualify prospects?
options: To avoid wasting time on people without the potential to buy
To check their qualifications for a job
questions.explain: Qualifying questions separate real prospects from others.
questions.evidence: Salespeople can avoid wasting time and increase their productivity by qualifying all prospects.

questions.q: Can selling be learned?
options: Yes: selling is a process with steps professional salespeople use
Only by people who studied law
questions.explain: Experts have spelled out the steps of the selling process.
questions.evidence: The Selling Process Selling is a process that can be learned.

questions.q: What are sales promotions?
options: Marketing events or sales efforts, other than advertising, personal selling and PR, that stimulate buying
questions.explain: They make personal selling and advertising more effective.
questions.evidence: Sales promotions are marketing events or sales efforts—not including traditional advertising, personal selling, and public relations—that stimulate buying.

questions.q: Who is trade sales promotion directed to?
options: Members of the marketing channel, such as wholesalers and retailers
questions.explain: Consumer sales promotion targets the ultimate consumer.
questions.evidence: Trade sales promotion is directed to members of the marketing channel, such as wholesalers and retailers.

questions.q: Which sales promotions often entice shoppers to try a different brand?
options: Cents-off coupons, free samples or an eye-catching in-store display
questions.explain: These are consumer sales promotions.
questions.evidence: Cents-off coupons, free samples, or an eye-catching display in a store will often entice shoppers to try a different brand.

questions.q: What is price skimming?
options: Launching a new product at a high price and lowering it over time
Launching at a low price to win market share
questions.explain: A high introductory price can create an image of quality and prestige.
questions.evidence: Price Skimming The practice of introducing a new product on the market with a high price and then lowering the price over time is called price skimming.

questions.q: Which pricing strategies are used for new products?
questions.explain: Leader pricing and bundling may be used for established products too.
questions.evidence: Price skimming and penetration pricing are strategies used in pricing new products; other strategies such as leader pricing and bundling may be used for established products as well.

questions.q: What is one advantage of penetration pricing?
options: It always gives the highest profit per item
It may discourage competitors from entering the market
It creates an image of luxury
questions.explain: It needs more planning because of mass production and marketing.
questions.evidence: Second, penetration pricing may discourage competitors from entering the market.

questions.q: Why does penetration pricing need more planning than skimming?
options: It is illegal in most countries
The company must gear up for mass production and marketing
It sells only to other companies
questions.explain: Low prices only work at high volume.
questions.evidence: Penetration pricing requires more extensive planning than skimming does because the company must gear up for mass production and marketing.

questions.q: How does the lesson divide the major types of retailers?
questions.explain: Nonstore retailing includes vending and online selling.
questions.evidence: The major types of retailers are described in Table 12.1 , which divides them into two main categories: in-store and nonstore retailing.

questions.q: What share of retail sales comes from fewer than 10 percent of retail businesses?
questions.explain: Giant retailers make most sales even though most retailers are small.
questions.evidence: Half of all retail sales come from fewer than 10 percent of all retail businesses.

questions.q: How has online retailing affected retailers?
options: More opportunity for smaller retailers and more competition for larger ones
questions.explain: Online trends have significantly impacted retailing.
questions.evidence: In recent years, online retailing trends have significantly impacted retailing organizations, providing more opportunity for smaller retailers and more competition for larger retailers.

questions.q: What are atmospherics in retailing?
options: The image of the store, or of the platform for nonstore retailing
questions.explain: For nonstore retailers the platform can be a website or vending machine.
questions.evidence: It also includes atmospherics—the image of the actual retailing store (or, in the case of nonstore retailing, the platform from which the product is offered, such as a website or vending machine).

questions.q: What does a small-business marketing plan describe?
options: The actions you'll take to persuade potential customers to buy
questions.explain: It turns your marketing strategy into action.
questions.evidence: It describes the actions you’ll take to persuade potential customers to buy your products or services.

questions.q: What is one of the best ways to stay on schedule and on budget with marketing?
questions.explain: Marketing takes time, money and preparation.
questions.evidence: One of the best ways to stay on schedule and on budget is to make a marketing plan.

questions.q: Which of these is given as a common marketing and sales goal?
options: Increase email subscribers, grow market share or increase sales by a certain percent
questions.explain: Describe your goals for the next year in the plan.
questions.evidence: Common marketing and sales goals are to increase email subscribers, grow market share, or increase sales by a certain percent.

questions.q: How should you check whether your marketing works?
options: Count how many adverts you placed
Compare your marketing and sales costs to the revenue it generates
questions.explain: Be consistent in how you measure effectiveness.
questions.evidence: Measure and update your plan Plan to compare your marketing and sales costs to the revenue it generates.

questions.q: What do you need to accept credit and debit cards?
options: A merchant services account with a bank or an account with a payment processing company
A government licence for each card
questions.explain: Online payments also carry fees.
questions.evidence: Credit cards To accept credit and debit cards, you’ll need either a merchant services account with a bank or an account with an independent payment processing company.

questions.q: What should the budget section of a marketing plan contain?
options: A complete breakdown of the costs of your marketing plan
questions.explain: Budgets keep marketing on track.
questions.evidence: Budget Include a complete breakdown of the costs of your marketing plan.

questions.q: According to GOV.UK, what must all marketing and advertising be?
options: Accurate, legal, decent, truthful, honest and socially responsible
questions.explain: Regulations and codes restrict what advertisers can do.
questions.evidence: Overview All marketing and advertising must be: an accurate description of the product or service legal decent truthful honest socially responsible

questions.q: How must you describe your product or service?
options: As positively as possible, whatever the truth
questions.explain: Descriptions must not mislead customers.
questions.evidence: You must describe your product or service accurately.

questions.q: What does the CAP non-broadcast code cover?
options: Non-broadcast advertising such as print and online, sales promotion and direct marketing
questions.explain: There are two advertising codes of practice.
questions.evidence: Non-broadcast media The CAP non-broadcast code has rules that cover non-broadcast advertising (for example print, online), sales promotion and direct marketing (such as telesales and email).

questions.q: How long can customers cancel an online or distance order after delivery, under the UK rules described?
questions.explain: They do not need to give a reason.
questions.evidence: You must tell the customer they can cancel their order up to 14 days after their order is delivered.

questions.q: What happens if you do not tell the customer about their right to cancel?
options: They lose the right to cancel
They can cancel at any time in the next 12 months
questions.explain: Telling them later starts a new 14-day period.
questions.evidence: If you do not tell the customer about their right to cancel, they can cancel at any time in the next 12 months.

questions.q: Do customers need to give a reason for cancelling a distance order?
options: Only if the item is faulty
Only if they paid by card
questions.explain: The right to cancel needs no reason.
questions.evidence: They do not need to give a reason for cancelling.

questions.q: When must you offer a full refund?
options: If an item is faulty, not as described or doesn't do what it's supposed to
Only if the customer has a receipt from last year
questions.explain: In some cases a change of mind also qualifies.
questions.evidence: You must offer a full refund if an item is faulty, not as described or does not do what it’s supposed to.

questions.q: Do customers have the same refund rights for items bought in a sale?
options: No, sale items can never be refunded
Only if the sale lasted a week
Yes, exactly the same as at full price
questions.explain: Sales do not reduce customers' rights.
questions.evidence: Customers have exactly the same rights to refunds when they buy items in a sale as when they buy them at full price.

questions.q: Is it legal to display a sign saying you do not accept returns or offer refunds?
options: Yes, if the sign is large
No: it's illegal to restrict or mislead customers about their rights
questions.explain: Customers' statutory rights cannot be taken away.
questions.evidence: It’s illegal to restrict or take away customers’ rights or to mislead them about their rights, for example by displaying a sign that says you do not accept returns or offer refunds.
